questions.statement: What is the past form of "to be" for the subject "They"?
questions.context: Identifying the past of the verb "to be" for plural subjects.

options.feedback: Correct! "Were" is the past plural form.

questions.explanation:
The student identifies the basic past conjugation of the verb "to be".

questions.statement: "We ________ (play) video games when the teacher ________ (come) in."
questions.context: Combining Simple and Continuous past tenses.

options.feedback: Correct! Long action (were playing) interrupted by a short action (came).
Incorrect. Both cannot be continuous if one is an interruption.

questions.explanation:
The student applies the "interrupted action" rule using both Past Simple and Past Continuous.

questions.statement: What is true about Mateo's project?
questions.context:
A text about a student's project.
"Last month, Mateo worked on a science project. He didn't sleep much because he was very busy. Finally, he finished the project and got an A."

options.text: He was lazy and slept a lot.
options.feedback: Incorrect. He "didn't sleep much" because he was busy.

options.text: His hard work resulted in a good grade.
options.feedback: Correct! Being busy and not sleeping (hard work) led to getting an "A" (good grade).

options.text: He worked on the project last week.
options.feedback: Incorrect. He worked on it "last month".

questions.explanation:
The student applies reading strategies to identify facts and outcomes in a past narrative.

questions.statement: Choose the correct question about a past action.
questions.context: Forming a question in the Past Simple.

options.text: Did you went to the party?
Did you go to the party?

options.feedback: Incorrect. Formal questions need the auxiliary first.

options.text: Was you go to the party?
options.feedback: Incorrect. "Was" is not the auxiliary for "go".

questions.explanation:
The student applies the correct auxiliary and verb form for a past tense question.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What was happening simultaneously in Márquez's life according to the text?
questions.context:
Analyzing biographical facts.
"Gabriel García Márquez (1927-2014) was a Nobel Prize winner. He wrote 'One Hundred Years of Solitude' while he was living in Mexico."

options.text: He was winning the Nobel Prize and living in Mexico.
He was living in Mexico and writing his famous book.
options.feedback: Correct! "Wrote... while he was living" shows simultaneous actions.

options.text: He was born in Mexico and died in 1927.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Dates and locations are wrong.

options.text: He only wrote books when he was in Aracataca.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Mexico is mentioned for this book.

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes the relationship between two events using the "while" structure in a biography.

questions.context: Correcting a complex sentence with multiple past tenses.

options.text: While I was walking home, it start raining and I didn't have an umbrella.
While I walked home, it was starting to rain and I wasn't have an umbrella.
While I was walking home, it started to rain and I didn't have an umbrella.
options.feedback: Correct! Continuous background, simple past interruption, and correct negative.

options.text: While I am walking home, it starts raining and I didn't had an umbrella.

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes and identifies the correct combination of past tenses and negative structures in a complex sentence.

questions.statement: Which word best describes the nature of the events mentioned?
questions.context:
Evaluating a summary of a narrative sequence.
"First, the team practiced every day. Then, they traveled to the tournament in Cali. Finally, they played the final match and became champions."

options.feedback: Correct! The events follow a clear chronological and logical order (practice -> travel -> play).
Incorrect. The sequence reaches a clear conclusion (became champions).

questions.explanation: The student evaluates the overall structure and flow of a past tense narrative to identify its logical characteristic.
